idiom_name: private field of the smallest component class (Blazor @code block, code-behind or per-screen ViewModel); framework scopes re-render to the owning component
implementation_notes: The state cell is an ordinary private field of the smallest class that uses it: a Blazor component's @code block, a window or page code-behind, or a small per-screen ViewModel. Nothing framework-specific is needed to declare it - what the framework contributes is that Blazor re-renders the component whose state changed (and its children), so a private field behaves like a colocated state cell. The replacement for the classic structure is this field-in-the-owner arrangement; DI singletons, static fields and application-level state services take the place of a global store and should be reserved for state that really is application-wide (session, cache, cross-route data). Move the value to a shared ViewModel or state container at the closest common owner when a second screen or component must read it, and keep transient UI state out of singletons so it cannot leak between users or circuits.
pitfalls: A static field, or a singleton registered in DI, is the app-wide store equivalent: shared across components, sessions and (on the server) circuits, so transient UI state placed there leaks between users.

State changes must run through a path that triggers rendering (an event handler or an explicit StateHasChanged call); mutating a field from a background loop renders nothing until something else re-renders the component.

Component state is discarded when the component is disposed or navigated away; values that must survive need PersistentComponentState or a scoped service, and capturing the component in such a service keeps the whole component alive.
